name: Convergent Thinking
description: Deriving the single best answer through speed, accuracy, logic, and systematic application of stored knowledge and standard decision-making procedures (Guilford; Cropley, 2006)

steps.name: Accumulate Stored Information - Recognize the familiar and gather existing knowledge
steps.description:
Recall and accumulate all relevant existing knowledge, familiar patterns, and established techniques that apply to the problem domain.

Per Cropley (2006), convergent thinking 'focuses on recognizing the familiar, reapplying techniques, and accumulating stored information.' It is 'most effective in situations where an answer readily exists and simply needs to be either recalled or worked out through decision making strategies.' This step gathers the knowledge base from which the single best answer will be derived.

SearchMemories.reason: Accumulate stored information by searching the knowledge graph for relevant prior knowledge, established patterns, and applicable techniques

BuildContext.reason: Recognize the familiar by building context around the problem domain to surface related concepts and existing solutions

stop_conditions: All relevant existing knowledge accumulated and cataloged
Familiar patterns and reapplicable techniques identified
Problem domain recognized as one where a definite answer exists or can be worked out
next_actions: Proceed to organize and structure the accumulated information

steps.name: Organize and Structure Information - Create analytical framework
steps.description:
Organize the accumulated ideas and information into a structured framework suitable for systematic evaluation.

Per Lundsteen, after divergent idea generation, 'ideas and information are organized and structured using convergent thinking.' Convergent thinking also 'involves manipulating existing knowledge by means of standard procedures' (Cropley, 2006). This step creates the structured scaffold for applying decision-making strategies.

SearchMemories.reason: Find existing organizational frameworks and standard procedures that may apply to structuring the information

stop_conditions: Information organized into clear categories or evaluation dimensions
Candidate solutions identified and enumerated from the accumulated knowledge
Standard procedures for evaluation identified and ready to apply

steps.name: Apply Decision-Making Strategies - Use knowledge, logic, and probabilities
steps.description:
Consciously apply standards, knowledge, logic, probabilities, and established decision-making strategies to evaluate the structured candidate solutions.

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Per Lundsteen, when using convergent/critical thinking to solve a problem, one 'consciously uses standards or probabilities to make judgments.' Apply 'knowledge, logic, probabilities and other decision-making strategies' systematically to each candidate. Convergent thinking emphasizes speed, accuracy, and logic (Cropley, 2006).

SequentialThinking.reason: Systematic application of decision-making strategies (knowledge, logic, probabilities, standards) to each candidate requires structured step-by-step reasoning

SearchMemories.reason: Find precedents, standards, and probabilistic evidence to apply as decision-making criteria

stop_conditions: All candidates evaluated using knowledge, logic, and probabilities
Standards or probabilities applied consistently as judgment criteria
Decision-making strategies explicitly documented for each assessment
Minority viewpoints considered before dismissal to guard against convergent thinking bias (Wikipedia critique: convergent thinkers may 'fail to appropriately evaluate minority opinion')
next_actions: Proceed to evaluate each solution individually

steps.name: Evaluate Solutions Individually - Assess each candidate in focused search
steps.description:
Evaluate each remaining candidate solution individually, searching for the single best answer with emphasis on speed, accuracy, and logic.

🧠 SEQUENTIAL THINKING REQUIRED: Use the SequentialThinking tool to work through this systematically.

Per Lundsteen, 'solutions are evaluated individually in a search for a single best answer.' For each candidate: Is this answer correct? Is it accurate? Does it satisfy all constraints? Convergent thinking demands that 'answers are either right or wrong' — assess each solution on that basis.

SequentialThinking.reason: Individual evaluation of each solution for correctness and constraint satisfaction requires focused serial reasoning — the core convergent thinking operation

stop_conditions: Every candidate solution evaluated individually for correctness
Speed, accuracy, and logic applied as evaluation criteria per Cropley (2006)
Solutions ranked by how well they meet all constraints
Weak or incorrect solutions eliminated with documented rationale
next_actions: Proceed to derive the single best answer

steps.name: Derive Single Best Answer - Select the unambiguous correct solution
steps.description:
Select the single best answer from the evaluation, leaving no room for ambiguity.

Per Wikipedia, 'a critical aspect of convergent thinking is that it leads to a single best answer, leaving no room for ambiguity. In this view, answers are either right or wrong. The solution that is derived at the end of the convergent thinking process is the best possible answer the majority of the time.'

WriteMemory.reason: Document the single best answer with complete decision rationale traceable through the full evaluation chain

stop_conditions: Single best answer selected — unambiguous, right-or-wrong determination made
Decision rationale traceable through the full evaluation chain
Answer verified as best possible solution given accumulated knowledge and applied standards
next_actions: Document final answer and proceed to implementation
